edges.identifiability_theorem: PROOF_LANE_FIRST_PASS: with R friction, S other resistance and C cutting, F1 - F2 = C1 holds exactly iff (R1 - R2) + (S1 - S2) - C2 = 0. Equal friction alone is insufficient unless the other terms are handled. After nuisance corrections the two total-force records identify C1 + (R1 - R2); neither the friction difference nor its ratio is separately identifiable. One independent scalar observation suffices when the nuisance terms are known, and a further total-force passage does not. Simultaneous tip-force measurement on both passages identifies the friction difference; pure cutting additionally requires the first-pass non-cutting tip load. Non-identifiability is witnessed, not asserted: 13104 indistinguishable pairs at observation error exactly zero, no scoped proposition falsified
edges.third_correction_2026_10_04: the first-passage forward friction is NOT missing. It is printed in the source's own Fig. 6 under the wrong name. In the post-penetration segment, where the needle has passed through and no material lies ahead of the tip, the cutting term is identically zero on BOTH passages, so the measured force is pure shaft-tissue friction and the ratio F1/F2 IS the passage friction ratio. Measured: 0.349 +/- 0.018 N first passage against 0.241 +/- 0.004 N second, ratio 1.4481, which this coordinator recomputed together with its propagated dispersion: 1.448 +/- 0.078, i.e. 5.71 sigma from unity. So friction is NOT equal across passages -- the edge's original assumption is refuted with a number, not just its stated reason
edges.proof_lane_theorem_scope_narrowed: PROOF_LANE_FIRST_PASS's non-identifiability holds only where a cutting term exists. The penetration mark in the source (I_d about 22.6 mm in Fig. 6, about 24 mm in Fig. 7, section 3.2 '10~23 mm') marks where it vanishes. Past it the identity needs a cutting term that is identically zero, so it does not apply and the quantity is identified on that segment. The theorem is right about the scalar coefficient and wrong about the force. Both halves are now carried
